name: pt-qwen
goal: photo_tools (image_convert) wave 1: Qwen authors ascii.rs (M), junction.rs (S), edges.rs (M), contour.rs (M). First Rust campaigns: measure which scope suits each member. S small, M exact/byte-exact, L largest algorithm, C crate-facing with the API card.

tasks.instructions: Byte-exact. grid: clamp columns to 1..=width, then cell_h = 2 * cell_w unless the image is shorter. Means truncate. In ANSI mode the reset comes once per line, after the last character, before the newline. Write the module once, in one reply; do not restate the contract.
tasks.test_instructions: Compare whole strings; include the truncating-mean case, ignored pixels past the last cell, and the ANSI layout.

tasks.instructions: Do the neighbour arithmetic in i64 (x - 1 at x == 0). OUTSIDE is its own value. Walk every table row, especially the saddle and the two-labels-but-not-a-checkerboard rows. Write the module once, in one reply; do not restate the contract.
tasks.test_instructions: Use the table rows; include border vertices, a saddle, a straight split and an L corner.

tasks.instructions: One slot per possible edge, index vertex_index * 4 + direction, holding the owning label; iterate slots in index order for both functions. Linking: right, else straight, else left; never back. Walk the hole, saddle and L-shape examples. Write the module once, in one reply; do not restate the contract.
tasks.test_instructions: Use the worked examples; check edge order at a shared vertex and that every edge lands in exactly one loop.

tasks.instructions: Assembly only: call crate::edges::raw_loops and crate::junction::is_junction (re-exported with `pub use`). Keep corners and junctions, rotate to the smallest (y, x) point (tie: smaller following point), sort by label, first point, second point. Write the module once, in one reply; do not restate the contract.
tasks.test_instructions: Use the worked examples as tests, plus is_junction through the re-export. Compare whole Vec<Loop> values.
